https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026.text: Five men have been arrested and three vans are being examined by army bomb disposal experts. Photograph: BBC View image in fullscreen Five men have been arrested and three vans are being examined by army bomb disposal experts. Photograph: BBC UK news Five arrested on terrorism charges after explosives found near RAF base used by US Counter-terrorism police investigate whether Iran is behind suspected bomb plot after member of public calls 999 over suspicious vehicles Jamie Grierson , Vikram Dodd and Helena Horton Sun 27 Sep 2026 14.49 EDT Last modified on Sun 27 Sep 2026 15.59 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Counter-terrorism police are investigating whether Iran is behind a suspected bomb plot after armed officers found explosives on three vans parked minutes from an RAF base used by the US military. The Guardian understands that after five men were arrested on terrorism charges, investigators were examining materials found in the vans, with an initial view being they were consistent with improvised explosive devices. Images circulating on Sunday showed shirtless men being handcuffed in a dark country lane in the early hours of Sunday after police were called to reports of three suspicious vans travelling towards RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire, which hosts US air force missions against Iran. The suspected plot appears to have been foiled by chance when a member of the public spotted unusual behaviour late at night in the countryside from a group of men and called 999. Emergency teams deploy bomb disposal robot at RAF Fairford air base During the major incident the residents of 85 households in the Cotswolds village of Whelford were rapidly evacuated to Cirencester leisure centre and a 400m cordon was placed around the white vans as robots from the army’s bomb squad examined them. Tests were ongoing to find out whether the suspected explosive devices were viable, with bomb robots deployed in the Gloucestershire countryside as investigations continued. View image in fullscreen Armed police man a roadblock while posted outside RAF Fairford base in Fairford, south-west England on 27 September 2026. Photograph: Justin Tallis/AFP/Getty Images After their initial arrest over explosives offences, the five men detained early on Sunday were further arrested later in the day on suspicion of the preparation of a terrorist act. The pictures of the men with their shirts off could point to a precautionary measure against the risk of suicide vests or concealed weapons. At least one van carried the logo of a fuel company and a phone number missing a digit. A real fuel company of the same name firmly rejected any connection to the incident and said: “We are extremely concerned that our company’s name has been used without our knowledge or permission.” It said it was cooperating with the authorities. In a statement, counter-terrorism police said: “At around 12.45am today (Sunday 27 September), police received a call relating to three suspicious vehicles which appeared to be travelling towards the airbase. View image in fullscreen Police moved on the three vans after a 999 call from a resident who spotted them as she drove home. Photograph: BBC news “Armed officers responded and five men were arrested in the Whelford area on suspicion of committing offences under the Explosives Act. They were further arrested on suspicion of preparation of a terrorist act, contrary to section 5 of the Terrorism Act.” The arrests come as the war between the US and Iran limps on. In July Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps noted RAF Fairford’s use by US bombers, warning the UK that “any base used for aggression against Iranian territory constitutes a legitimate target for our forces”. Counter-terror police and the security services are searching for the motive. The circumstances of the arrest near the base and prior warnings from Tehran leave an Iranian motive high in the investigators’ and government’s thinking. But sources warn nothing is being ruled out, including a jihadist or other motive, and the UK threat level remains at severe, the second highest, meaning an attack is highly likely. location map Whether there was any foreign involvement forms part of the investigation, and Iran’s ministry of intelligence and security has orchestrated attacks overseas before. Any proven link with Iran would be a dramatic escalation in hostilities between the UK and Tehran. While several recent incidents in the UK have been linked to the Middle-Eastern country, including the antisemitic arson attack on four Hatzola ambulances in Golders Green , the alleged plot at RAF Fairford appears to be significantly more serious. And it raises urgent questions for the UK security services after it appeared the authorities had been unaware of the alleged plot, with police only moving on the three vans after a 999 call from a resident who spotted them as she drove home. View image in fullscreen RAF Fairford is a military base that hosts US air force bombers involved in the Iran conflict. Photograph: Getty Images The US president, Donald Trump, claimed to have had the suspects under view for a “long time” and alleged the men “were looking to do big damage” – although the Guardian understands the operation was not intelligence-led, suggesting investigators had not known about any potential plot in advance. “It was fantastic. Working with Britain, it was an amazing job,” Trump said. The UK prime minister, Andy Burnham, was being updated on the matter from Liverpool, where the Labour party conference is taking place. He cancelled plans to take part in a journalists versus politicians football match in order to take calls about the incident. He said it was “deeply concerning” and the government will “always take every step necessary” to protect people. View image in fullscreen A B‑1B Lancer bomber parked at the RAF Fairford airbase, which hosts US air force personnel, in Fairford, Gloucestershire, Britain, 27 September 2026. Photograph: Toby Shepheard/Reuters Fairford has a particularly long runway, which extends almost 2 miles (3km). It is reinforced to support heavy bombers such as the B-1 and B-52, which have been deployed in attacks on Iran. The aircraft are capable of carrying large payloads, including “bunker buster” bombs. In March this year, after then prime minister, Sir Keir Starmer, granted permission for “defensive” US action against Iranian missile sites from UK bases, four American bombers landed at RAF Fairford and the US started using British bases for “specific defensive operations”. There have been protests in recent months over the UK government’s decision to allow the US to use RAF Fairford to carry out strikes on Iranian missile sites that are attacking ships in the strait of Hormuz. At the time of Iran’s warning in July, a government spokesperson said: “Our armed forces are ready to keep the United Kingdom safe from any kind of attacks, whether it’s on our soil or from abroad. The UK stands ready 24/7 to defend itself.” Evacuated residents of Whelford spoke of “heightened tensions” in recent weeks around the base with more frequent, visible police patrols. Outside Cirencester leisure centre, Jason, a resident of Whelford who declined to give his surname, said: “There have been heightened tensions recently around the base, we are aware it is used by the USAF … It always feels pretty safe. Some residents have seen increased police patrols.” View image in fullscreen Residents of the Cotswolds village of Whelford were evacuated to Cirencester leisure centre. Photograph: Getty Images It was unclear when people would be able to return to their normal lives; those at the leisure centre said they had been asked by authorities if they had anywhere else to stay on Sunday night. The Fairford youth football club, about 1.5 miles (2.4km) north-west of Whelford, was taken over as a temporary base for the emergency service response to the incident. There were several police vehicles, ambulances, fire engines, pop-up tents and a large mobile command-unit vehicle in the grounds. View image in fullscreen Fairford youth football club. Photograph: Toby Shepheard/Reuters Richard Ocone, the assistant chief constable with Gloucestershire constabulary, said: “We appreciate the disruption this will have caused and would like to reassure them we are working as quickly as we can to get them back in their properties.” Explore more on these topics UK news England news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed UK UK politics Education Media Society Law Scotland Wales Northern Ireland

https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/o.text: Downed power lines in the aftermath of Hurricane Isaias in Milton, Florida, on Saturday. Photograph: Gerald Herbert/AP View image in fullscreen Downed power lines in the aftermath of Hurricane Isaias in Milton, Florida, on Saturday. Photograph: Gerald Herbert/AP Hurricane Isaias Thousands without power in Florida and Alabama as Isaias moves north At least four deaths linked to storm amid warnings of flash flooding that could stretch into Appalachians Associated Press Sun 11 Oct 2026 09.45 EDT Last modified on Sun 11 Oct 2026 09.46 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Nearly 396,000 customers across the Florida Panhandle and southern Alabama remained without power early Sunday as remnants of Hurricane Isaias moved north, where widespread moderate to heavy rainfall was expected across the central Appalachians and mid-Atlantic region. Four dead as Isaias weakens to post-tropical cyclone after striking Florida panhandle Read more Heavy rainfall associated with the storm could bring isolated flash flooding and strong wind gusts and remain a threat across the south-eastern US, especially near the southern Appalachians, according to the National Weather Service (NWS). That could bring scattered power outages and downed trees and power lines. Life-threatening surf and rip current conditions were expected to continue along the Gulf and south-eastern Atlantic coasts. At least four deaths were linked to the storm, including two people killed when trees fell on to homes in Florida and Alabama . Forecasters warned that flooding could stretch into the Appalachians. Isaias came ashore as a category 2 hurricane on Friday near Destin, Florida , a Gulf Coast vacation spot filled with high-rises and tourist shops. Despite warnings of storm surges ahead of the storm, several major routes along the coast were open by daybreak on Saturday and free of downed trees and power lines typically seen after major hurricanes. Hurricane-force winds in the Florida Panhandle blew the roof off a Pensacola hotel, and the city’s mayor said the airport “took some damage”. The storm flattened a boathouse in Destin and ripped away part of the facade of a high-rise in Panama City Beach. In Florida’s Escambia county, sheriff Chip Simmons said a woman was killed when a tree fell on her home – and a man died of carbon monoxide fumes from a generator running in his garage. Four of the man’s family members, ranging in age from 4 to 72, were treated but were expected to survive, the sheriff said. The first hurricane of the Atlantic season, Isaias roared farther into Alabama with tropical-force winds. One person died when a tree fell on a house in Birmingham, the city’s fire chief, Cory Moon, said. A second storm-related death in Alabama was attributed to a motor vehicle crash involving a downed tree in Barbour county, said Josh Johnson of the state’s emergency management agency. Along Alabama’s Gulf Coast, authorities in Mobile reported numerous downed trees and power lines. Donald Trump approved an emergency declaration for Georgia after the president did the same for Florida and Alabama, allowing for federal aid. The US Energy Department authorized emergency exchanges of crude oil from the nation’s strategic petroleum reserve to address disruptions in supply because of the storm. The NWS said parts of Georgia and the Carolinas could see heavy rain capable of causing flash floods. Meanwhile, in the Pacific, Simon strengthened to 155mph (250kph), only just below the threshold for becoming a category 5 storm, as it approached Mexico’s coast. Simon was expected to bring heavy rainfall beginning on Sunday to parts of south-western Mexico with life-threatening flooding and mudslides. Tropical storm Rachel was also expected to bring heavy winds and rain to northern Mexico and southern California. https://nltimes.nl/2026/10/09/dutch-bicy.text: Image AMSTERDAM, NETHERLANDS - NOVEMBER 10: Babboe bicycle added to transport loads on November 10, 2014 in Amsterdam. - Credit: Kefirm / DepositPhotos - License: All Rights Reserved Business Babboe Accell Group Singapore Batavus Koga covid-19 pandemic Hungary Germany » More tags « Less tags Share this article: Opens in a new window Opens in a new window Opens in a new window Opens in a new window Opens in a new window Opens in a new window Dutch bicycle brands Batavus, KOGA, and Babboe to continue under new Singaporean owner Friday, 9 October 2026 - 19:30 Dutch bicycle brands Batavus, KOGA, and Babboe are set to resume operations under new ownership. The administrators overseeing the bankruptcy of bicycle manufacturer Accell are selling the rights to the three brands to investment company Dutech. The deal also includes Accell’s IT platform and Hungarian operations, as well as potentially some of its staff. Singapore-based Dutech owns several brands in the bicycle and security sectors, including German bicycle brands Kreidler and Prophete. The company employs 3,100 people worldwide. Dutech had long been rumored to be the frontrunner to acquire Accell’s brands. The financial terms of the deal have not been disclosed. Accell was declared bankrupt in August after running into financial trouble in the aftermath of the Covid-19 pandemic, when it was left with large stocks of unsold bicycles. The company also faced other setbacks, including a major recall of Babboe cargo bikes. Since the bankruptcy, the administrators have spent months examining the possibilities for restarting parts of the business under new ownership. Several parties initially showed interest in acquiring Accell, which employs around 2,000 people, but many were only interested in specific parts of the business. At the end of last month, 12GO Biking, one of the Netherlands’ largest bicycle retailers, was announced as the buyer of Accell’s bicycle stock. The latest deal covers the rights to the brands. The administrators said the agreement secures the future of the well-known Dutch names. “They will remain on the market and be further developed by Dutech,” they said. A spokesperson could not immediately clarify what the takeover means for customers who still have warranties on bicycles from the brands. Many details of the deal remain unresolved, including how many Accell employees will retain their jobs. The IT platform will be transferred to Dutech at a later stage, as the administrators are still using it to settle the bankruptcy. Negotiations are also continuing over the sale of other parts of the business, including the spare parts division. The administrators expect to share more information when further details become available. https://www.digi24.ro/stiri/externe/ue/n.text: Liderii europeni au respins eforturile lui Vladimir Putin de a reforma arhitectura de securitate a continentului în cadrul negocierilor de pace privind Ucraina, în timp ce Volodimir Zelenski i-a avertizat pe aliați că Washingtonul și Moscova discutau deja această chestiune, relatează Financial Times . Trimisul special al SUA, Steve Witkoff, și ginerele lui Donald Trump, Jared Kushner, s-au întâlnit joi la Moscova cu președintele rus, în urma discuțiilor de pace privind Ucraina care au avut loc la Abu Dhabi la începutul acestei săptămâni, unde delegația rusă a adus în discuție aspectele legate de securitatea Europei, refuzând totodată să se întâlnească cu oficialii europeni. „Nu este nevoie să reinventăm roata. Europa a avut o arhitectură de securitate europeană funcțională până când aceasta a fost mai întâi subminată treptat și, în cele din urmă, distrusă de invazia Rusiei în Ucraina”, a declarat președintele Consiliului European, Antonio Costa, care i-a primit joi la Dublin pe președintele ucrainean și pe alți lideri. Liderul de la Kiev a declarat că negocierile dintre SUA, Rusia și Ucraina, care au avut loc săptămâna aceasta la Abu Dhabi, au inclus „multe discuții despre garanțiile de securitate”. „Europa trebuie să acorde cu adevărat atenție acestui aspect”, a declarat Zelenski. „Când americanii și rușii discută despre aceste chestiuni, nu este vorba doar despre Ucraina; de fapt, este vorba mai degrabă despre un fel de nou cadru de securitate între Europa și Rusia. Și noi considerăm această abordare puțin ciudată”. Oficialii ruși au afirmat în repetate rânduri că aranjamentele de securitate ale continentului trebuie regândite — ceea ce înseamnă interzicerea extinderii în continuare a NATO și a exercițiilor militare în apropierea frontierei ruse, precum și retragerea trupelor și a echipamentului militar de pe flancul estic al NATO. Aceste cereri au fost interpretate în multe capitale europene ca o încercare a Kremlinului de a-și restabili sfera de influență și de a încălca suveranitatea națională a statelor membre ale UE și NATO. Joi, președintele rus Vladimir Putin a declarat că propunerile Moscovei privind o nouă arhitectură de securitate trebuie discutate înainte de a se ajunge la un acord privind încetarea războiului. „Ce ne spun europenii? Nu, abia după ce se va instaura pacea în Ucraina. Dar ei intenționează să trimită trupe acolo după ce se va instaura pacea în Ucraina. Asta înseamnă continuarea războiului”, a declarat Putin. Kushner și Witkoff i-au spus lui Putin, în cadrul unor declarații televizate, că Statele Unite doresc ca europenii să participe la viitoarele discuții privind războiul în care este implicată Rusia și că Washingtonul a inițiat discuții cu aliații europeni cu privire la arhitectura de securitate a continentului. O persoană la curent cu discuțiile de la Abu Dhabi a recunoscut că se făcea referire la această chestiune. „Da, se discută despre tema securității europene în sens larg. Dar nu și despre conținutul acesteia”, a spus persoana. „Inclusiv la Abu Dhabi”. Vladimir Medinski, principalul negociator al Rusiei, a declarat la televiziunea de stat, după discuțiile de la Abu Dhabi, că Rusia dorește să creeze „un nou sistem de securitate european cuprinzător, care să servească ca o nouă Ialta și un nou Potsdam”, înlocuind ordinea mondială stabilită după cel de-al Doilea Război Mondial. Trei oficiali au declarat pentru FT că în capitalele europene se simte o nervozitate tot mai mare la gândul că acceptarea unor discuții privind chestiuni mai ample de apărare și securitate la nivel continental ar fi prețul pe care ar trebui să-l plătească pentru a obține un loc la negocierile privind Ucraina, lucru pe care au refuzat să-l facă timp de cinci ani. Kristen Michal, prim-ministrul Estoniei, a avertizat că Europa a fost atrasă într-o „capcană” prin care s-a discutat despre arhitectura de securitate a continentului în schimbul unui rol în negocieri și că Putin a încercat de ani buni să-și impună influența asupra suveranității statelor membre ale NATO. Kaja Kallas, șefa diplomației UE, a declarat că Europa ar trebui să fie dispusă să înceapă discuțiile privind arhitectura de securitate a continentului numai după ce Rusia va accepta un acord de pace. „În acest moment, concentrarea atenției asupra arhitecturii de securitate europene deturnează, de fapt, atenția de la ceea ce ar trebui să fie cu adevărat prioritar, și anume încetarea focului care să pună capăt masacrelor din Ucraina”, a declarat Kallas. Neliniștea cu privire la negocierile privind securitatea europeană, manifestată de liderii continentului, a sporit presiunea pentru a pune capăt unei dezbateri de lungă durată cu privire la cine ar trebui să reprezinte Europa în eventualele negocieri. Liderii europeni vor dezbate această chestiune la Dublin, în speranța de a găsi un nume încă din această lună. Interacțiunea Europei cu negociatorii americani și ucraineni, precum și demersurile ad-hoc către Putin, au fost imprevizibile și, uneori, incoerente. Marea Britanie, Franța, Germania și Italia, alături de UE, au trimis toate delegații la întâlnirile organizate în marja discuțiilor de la Abu Dhabi din această săptămână. „Nu se poate discuta despre securitatea Europei fără ca Europa să aibă un cuvânt de spus la masa negocierilor”, a adăugat Costa. „Acest cuvânt de spus al Europei trebuie să fie rezultatul unui efort comun al națiunilor europene, al Uniunii Europene și al NATO”.
